page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The system provides 64 GiB of main memory, creating an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The x86_64 architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX and AVX-512F. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero GPUs included, and the instance provides no local storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistence. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect lower-tier computational capacity balanced by functional memory and instruction throughput. The processor achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 3502.0 and a single-core score of 920.0, while multi-core stress-ng tests reached 5855.73. Compression operations showed single-threaded gzip throughput of 19.04 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 26.37 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory write throughput measured an average 35.69 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance sustained 5.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.15 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Natural language inference on a lightweight 135M parameter model achieved 447.75 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 94.96 tokens/sec for generation.

Cost efficiency is centered around the instance's high RAM density per vCPU rather than pure compute throughput. Because computational benchmark figures fall into the lower quartiles, utilizing this instance for CPU-heavy tasks presents efficiency tradeoffs. It delivers effective resource allocation for memory-bound tasks requiring substantial memory residency without high CPU frequency. Recommended workloads include distributed in-memory caches, Redis databases, memory-centric batch data processing, and enterprise middleware needing ample operational memory.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU density, it is tailored for environments requiring large operational memory footprints relative to compute capacity. The instance relies entirely on remote storage, containing no local disks, and operates without GPU acceleration while maintaining a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance benchmarks reflect modest computational output, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 3502.0 and stress-ng score of 5855.73, alongside steady large-block uncached memory write bandwidth of 35.69 GB/sec and 5.79 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis deployments, and memory-intensive enterprise services that prioritize memory capacity over raw processor speeds.
